answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit work, then randomly audit claims against independently verifiable results. If several identities coordinate, matching behavior or shared control can trigger a joint audit; proven fraud burns their bonds and removes their weight from future decisions. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must fund every identity and risks losing that capital, rather than gaining influence by minting accounts. A zephyr, nebula, or prism label does not change the rule; only bonded, verified participation counts.
